q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to an 8-month-old for fever — it is not to be used in children younger than 6 months, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and know your child's weight before giving it [6]. You can also give acetaminophen (Tylenol) every 4 to 6 hours [6]. Never give aspirin to a child unless their provider says it is OK [6].

Keep breastfeeding or offering plenty of fluids as normal, and check on your child regularly, including during the night [3]. Give the medicine if your child is distressed or uncomfortable, and check the packaging or leaflet to make sure it is suitable, or speak to a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure [3]. Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
For vomiting, the main thing is to keep fluids going in so your son does not get dehydrated. Give him small sips of an oral rehydration solution, which you can buy without a prescription, according to MedlinePlus [1]. The NHS says to give regular small sips of rehydration solution to replace lost fluids, and to ask a pharmacist to recommend one [5]. Small amounts more often work better than a large drink at once [5].

Do not give young children fruit juice or fizzy drinks, as these can make vomiting worse [5]. Sports drinks can help with mild dehydration, but they may not replace the important nutrients and minerals that oral rehydration fluids do [4].

If you think he is severely dehydrated, call your doctor, according to the CDC [4].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the common causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is to keep fluids going in [3].

When your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, according to the SEUP [5]. Watch how well they take it; if they keep it down, you can slowly give it more often [5]. Don't use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids from the pharmacy are the most helpful for mild dehydration, and sports drinks without caffeine can help mild cases too, according to the CDC [2].

See your doctor if your child is very drowsy, vomits many times, or won't take fluids [3], or if you think they are severely dehydrated [2].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in children with asthma, and it can also be the first sign of a cold or of croup [4][5][6]. Keep the room calm and let your child rest propped up a little; if the air is dry, a cool mist may help them settle.

If your child has asthma, use their inhaler as prescribed, and if they need it more often than usual, or the cough is waking them at night, see your doctor [4]. For a barking, seal-like cough with a hoarse voice or noisy breathing, ask for an urgent appointment, because medicine can shorten croup [5].

Get medical help right away if your child is breathing hard, gasping, or turning pale or blue, or if a cough bout leaves them struggling for breath [1][6].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days [6]. If the cough comes in bouts that are worse at night, or your son makes a "whoop" sound gasping between coughs, it may be whooping cough: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, the cough comes in bouts lasting a few minutes and may end in vomiting or a whoop [4]. The cough can then last several weeks or months [4].

Keep him comfortable and offer fluids often. If you think it could be whooping cough, ask your doctor — the first signs are like a cold, with a runny nose and sore throat, and a high temperature is uncommon [4].

Get urgent medical advice if he is getting worse or not getting better, or if he is struggling to breathe [3]. In babies under 3 months, coughing bouts, difficulty breathing or turning blue or grey need medical care right away [4].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without fever, with normal eating, is usually caused by a common infection like a cough or cold, according to the NHS [1]. There is nothing in the sources about treating a cough on its own, so no medicine is needed for it.

Keep offering fluids and normal meals; a poor appetite for a few days is not harmful [2]. If a fever does appear, the aim of treatment is comfort, not bringing the temperature right down, and paracetamol is the usual first choice, with the dose based on the child's weight [3][6].

Get help if your child has a high temperature that lasts 5 days or more, is not eating or is not their usual self, or has other signs of illness such as a rash along with a high temperature [1].

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots on the stomach that appear in one day are usually caused by a mild, short-lived illness, according to the SEUP [1]. Most such causes are benign and get better on their own [1].

Keep her comfortable and let her keep doing what she normally does [4]. Offer fluids often and watch her nappies or trips to the toilet [4]. Note when she last passed stool and what it looked like [4].

Get her seen if she is generally unwell, floppy, pale, or refusing food and drink [6]. Also get her checked if the spots do not fade when you press on them, or if she has a fever with them.

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, and most children recover quickly [1][6]. For a 6-year-old who fell from a bed, the SEUP says to watch for the warning signs over the first 24 hours after the knock [3].

If there is headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol in the dose your doctor indicates [6]. Let him rest, physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the blow was, with no sport and no screens, then return to normal activities gradually [4]. He can eat normally, and he can sleep — for a more significant knock, it is advisable to wake him every 4 hours [6].

Go to the emergency department if he has a severe or worsening headache that does not improve with the usual medicine, repeated vomiting, confusion or disorientation, behaviour changes, trouble speaking or walking, or blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears, according to the SEUP [4][5]. Also go if the fall was from more than one metre [5].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
Start with single vegetables and fruits: mashed or soft, cooked sticks of parsnip, broccoli, potato, yam, sweet potato, carrot, apple or pear, according to the NHS [4]. Include vegetables that are not sweet, like broccoli, cauliflower and spinach, so your baby gets used to a range of flavours [4]. Make sure any cooked food has cooled right down before you offer it [4].

At first, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to eating — they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [1]. Offer a variety of foods alongside their milk, and increase the amount and variety gradually [1].

Foods containing allergens, such as peanuts, hens' eggs, gluten and fish, can be introduced from around 6 months, one at a time and in small amounts so you can spot any reaction [4]. Full-fat dairy like pasteurised cheese and plain yoghurt can be given from around 6 months, with no added sugar [4]. Babies do not need salt or sugar added to their food or cooking water [4].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text: For a 9-month-old, breast milk or first infant formula should still be their main drink, and water is offered only in small sips with meals, according to the NHS [4]. Introduce a cup from around 6 months and offer sips of water with meals; an open cup or a free-flow cup without a valve helps them learn to sip and is better for their teeth [4]. Do not give whole cows', goats' or sheep's milk as a main drink until they are 1 year old [4]. If they are unwell, offer more fluids and more frequent breastfeeding [3].

text: It is common for babies to prefer fruit, and the CDC has tips to help picky eaters try new foods [1]. Keep offering vegetables alongside what they already like, and offer a variety of foods, including ones with bitter flavours such as broccoli, cauliflower, spinach and cabbage, according to the NHS [2]. q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text: At 13 months, formula is no longer needed — she can move to pasteurised whole cows' milk as her main drink, according to the NHS [3]. From 12 months she should be eating 3 meals a day plus 2 healthy snacks, with milk alongside rather than as most of her intake [3]. Offer a variety: starchy foods like potatoes, bread and rice; fruit and vegetables; full-fat dairy such as cheese and yoghurt; and protein from meat, fish, eggs, beans or lentils [3]. Choose full-fat dairy, since children under 2 need the vitamins and extra energy in it [3]. Keep giving milk in a cup with meals and snacks, and let her eat what the family eats in smaller portions [2][3]. If she was born prematurely, ask your doctor for advice on feeding [2].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby: the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one person to another, and it is not essential that a baby has a bowel movement every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more is the consistency — constipation is when stools become too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, and it may come with fewer bowel movements [6]. In a baby under 6 months, keep the usual feeding with breast milk or formula [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3]. See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, a lot of tummy pain, or the baby vomits many times and cannot keep down solids or liquids [3].

A cough that comes on mainly when he lies down can be a sign of asthma, which often causes coughing at night or early in the morning, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Asthma makes the airways inflamed and narrowed, which can cause coughing, wheezing and chest tightness [4].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Using a reliever inhaler more often than usual is a sign the asthma is not as well controlled as it should be, and it is a reason to see your doctor [2]. Asthma is treated with inhalers that either relieve symptoms or prevent them, and most people do well when the right treatment is used correctly [3][5].

Keep using the inhaler as your plan says, and make sure it is used correctly — a spacer makes an aerosol inhaler easier to use and helps the medicine reach the lungs [1]. A doctor, nurse or pharmacist can show you how to use it properly [3].

See your doctor if your son needs his inhaler more often, if his symptoms are not improving, or if they are waking him at night or stopping him doing his usual activities [2]. If he has an asthma attack, sit him up straight, stay calm, and use the reliever inhaler as set out in his action plan [4].

text:
A strange noise while breathing can be a sign of inflammation of the voice box and windpipe, which often starts like a cold and then causes hoarseness and a barking cough, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It can also be a whistling sound, which is more common with viral infections [5].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. Because your baby has had one before, a fever today does not mean it will happen again — you cannot prevent febrile seizures, and most do not need treatment [6].

What to do now: check the temperature with a digital thermometer under the arm, keeping it in place as long as the leaflet says [1]. If a seizure starts, do not move your child or hold them in place, and do not put anything in their mouth [5]. Time it: most last 2 to 3 minutes, and it is rare for them to last more than 10 minutes [2].

Get medical help if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, if breathing is difficult, if the stiffness and twitching are on only one side, if they are more sleepy than usual for more than an hour afterwards, or if there is more than one seizure within 24 hours [2].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious or likely to cause long-term harm [2]. Most febrile seizures do not need treatment, but a child needs to be checked in hospital after a first febrile seizure [3]. Febrile seizures are not the same thing as epilepsy; children who have had one have a slightly increased chance of epilepsy later, but this is rare [3].

If your child has another seizure, keep them safe while you wait for medical help: check the time it starts and ends, protect their head with your hands or something soft, and move dangerous objects away [4]. q: my child tested positive for COVID and has a fever
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and it usually settles within 1 to 4 days [1][3].

You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen if the fever is making them uncomfortable — paracetamol is usually the first choice [5]. The right amount depends on your child's age and weight, so follow the dose on the medicine's leaflet or ask your doctor or pharmacist. Never give aspirin to a child under 16 [7]. Call your doctor if the fever lasts 5 days or more, if your child is not eating or not themselves, or if they seem dehydrated — fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, no tears when crying [7]. Get emergency help now for a stiff neck, a rash that does not fade when pressed, drowsiness that is hard to wake, confusion, or difficulty breathing [7].

q: my son had croup last winter and now has a barking cough again
text:
A barking cough that comes on suddenly at night, after a few days of cold-like symptoms, is the usual pattern of croup, according to the SEUP [3]. Croup is an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe, usually caused by a virus, and most cases are mild and can be treated at home [1].

Keep your son calm and comfortable: crying or getting upset makes the noisy breathing worse [3]. Offer fluids if he has a fever and give his usual fever medicine [4]. Water can help ease the cough, whether he drinks it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [6]. Symptoms are usually worse at night and last about three to five days, though they can persist up to a week [1][4].

Watch his breathing and his colour and general condition, as these show if he is getting worse [4]. If you are worried about his breathing, call your doctor right away [1].

A rash that comes up after swimming in a lake is often hives — raised, itchy bumps or patches that can appear anywhere on the body and look pink or red on white skin, though the colour is harder to see on brown or black skin [1]. In childhood, most hives are caused by an infection, and an allergic cause is less common [4].

Get help straight away if their lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell, they struggle to breathe or swallow, their skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale, or they become limp, floppy or not responding as usual — these can be signs of a serious allergic reaction [7].

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
The most common early symptoms of malaria are fever, headache and chills, and they usually start within 10–15 days of being bitten by an infected mosquito [1][2]. Because these symptoms are not specific, getting tested early matters [2]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1].

If your child has fever, headache or chills after travelling to a malaria area, get them tested for malaria early — early treatment of mild malaria can stop it becoming severe [2].

Severe symptoms include extreme tiredness, impaired consciousness, multiple convulsions, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, jaundice, and abnormal bleeding; someone with these needs emergency care right away [2].

A brief pause in breathing during crying can be a breath-holding spell: the child gasps, exhales and stops breathing for a short time, and normal breathing starts again after a brief period [5]. q: my daughter fainted for a few seconds at school and feels fine now
text:
A short faint like this is called a syncope: a sudden, brief loss of consciousness that happens when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, according to the SEUP [2]. It often follows heat, pain, fear, anxiety, standing still for a long time, or getting up too quickly, and children usually recover within a couple of minutes after resting [2][5].

If she feels unwell again, have her sit or lie down straight away, breathe slowly and deeply, and get up slowly afterwards — first sitting, then standing after a few minutes [5]. It also helps children who faint easily to drink more fluids, especially with exercise [4].

See a doctor if the faint lasted more than 3 to 5 minutes before she came round, if it happened during exercise or while she was sitting, or if it came with palpitations, chest pain, jerking of the arms and legs, or passing urine [6].

Get help right away for neck pain, double vision, loss of consciousness, a seizure, repeated vomiting, a headache that is severe or getting worse, or weakness, tingling or burning in the arms or legs [2].

q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105°C is not possible — a thermometer reading that high means the thermometer is faulty or was misread, so check it again with a digital thermometer in the armpit [2]. A high temperature in a young child is very common and is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, chickenpox or tonsillitis, and it usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days [2][4].

You can usually look after them at home: give plenty of fluids, offer food if they want it, keep them at home, and check on them regularly, including during the night [3]. If they are distressed or uncomfortable, give either paracetamol or ibuprofen — check the leaflet to make sure the medicine suits your child, and do not alternate the two unless a doctor or nurse tells you to [3][4]. Do not sponge them down or wrap them in too many clothes [4].

Get medical advice if you are worried about your child, or if the paracetamol or ibuprofen is not helping [3].

q: my 5 year old won't stop itching her arms and legs at night
text:
Itching that is worse at night is a common sign of scabies, an itchy rash caused by mites that spreads through close skin contact and should be treated quickly to stop it spreading, according to the NHS [5]. The WHO describes scabies itch as severe and often worse at night, with itchy lines and bumps on the fingers, wrists, arms and legs [2]. Many other things can also cause itchy skin and rashes in children, so it is worth having your child looked at to be sure [5].

While you wait, keep their fingernails cut short and put socks on their hands at night to stop scratching, bathe them in cool water and pat the skin dry without rubbing, dress them in loose clothes, and ask a pharmacist about an antihistamine to help the itching [3][4]. Do not use ibuprofen unless a doctor tells you to, as it may cause serious skin infections [3][4].

q: how long does flu last in toddlers
text:
Most people recover from fever and other symptoms within a week without needing medical attention, according to the WHO [5]. The cough can be severe and may last 2 weeks or more [5].

While your toddler is ill: stay home to avoid infecting others, rest, and give plenty of fluids [4]. You can treat the fever or aches with over-the-counter medication [6]. Do not give over-the-counter cough and flu medicine to a child younger than 6 years old unless a health care provider advises it [6].

Seek medical care if symptoms get worse [4], or if there is trouble breathing or fast breathing, dehydration, fever lasting longer than 4 days, or symptoms lasting more than 10 days without getting better, according to the CDC [2].

q: my 14 year old says her throat hurts really bad when swallowing
text:
A sore throat that hurts when swallowing is usually caused by a virus, like a cold or flu, and normally gets better by itself within a week, according to the NHS [4][5]. Tonsillitis is another common cause in teenagers, with a sore throat and problems swallowing [2].

To help soothe it: drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck ice cubes, ice lollies or hard sweets, and rest [5]. Avoid smoking or smoky places [5]. Antibiotics are not normally needed, because they will not usually relieve symptoms or speed up recovery [7].

See a doctor if the sore throat does not improve after a week, or if there is a lump in the mouth or neck, or a mouth ulcer lasting more than 3 weeks [7]. Ask for an urgent appointment if you are worried, or if there is a very high temperature, shivering, or signs of dehydration such as peeing less than usual or dark, strong-smelling pee [7].

q: why do I have a fever and chills today
text:
A fever is a sign your body is fighting an infection, and chills often come with it — the SEUP says fever is usually caused by mild infections, especially viral ones, and it is a defence mechanism, not a sign of seriousness by itself [3]. The SEUP also lists chills and sweating as part of the picture [4].

Most fevers last 2 to 4 days, though they can last longer without being more serious [4]. Drink enough fluids to prevent dehydration, and if the fever is very high your doctor may suggest an over-the-counter medicine such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Adults can take aspirin, but children with fever should not [2].

If the fever lasts 5 days or more, or you feel very unwell, contact your doctor [7].

q: he has an inhaler but I dont know when to use it
text:
For most people, the main treatment for asthma is medicine breathed in with an inhaler, and it works well to reduce or prevent symptoms [2]. Which inhaler your son has decides when he uses it: a blue reliever is used only when he gets symptoms, a preventer is used every day to prevent them, and some inhalers (AIR or MART) are used both ways [2].

During an asthma attack, sit him up straight and try to stay calm. With a blue reliever inhaler, give 1 puff every 30 to 60 seconds until he feels better, up to 10 puffs, shaking the inhaler between puffs and using a spacer if you have one [1]. With an AIR or MART inhaler, give 1 puff every 1 to 3 minutes, up to 6 puffs [1]. If his own asthma action plan gives a different maximum, follow that plan [1].

Get urgent medical help if he starts to feel worse at any time, or does not feel better after the maximum dose [1].

text: It is common for a first tooth to appear between 4 and 8 months, but some babies get their first tooth later, according to MedlinePlus [3]. q: my child has chickenpox, when can he go back to school
text:
Chickenpox is very contagious, and a child is contagious from 1 to 2 days before the rash starts until all the spots have crusted over [3]. Children usually miss 5 to 6 days of school or childcare because of chickenpox [1].

Keep him home until every lesion has scabbed over, according to the CDC [3]. If he was vaccinated and gets chickenpox, the spots may not crust, and he stays contagious until no new spots have appeared for 24 hours [3].

For the itching, calamine lotion and oatmeal baths can help, and acetaminophen can treat the fever, MedlinePlus says [6]. Do not give aspirin for chickenpox, because that combination can cause Reye syndrome [6].

q: she bumped her forehead on the table and cried right away, do I need to watch her
text:
A bump on the forehead is often minor because the skull is hard and protects the brain, but it is worth watching closely, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Crying right away is common; what matters is how she is over the next hours and days, because concussion signs may not show up right away and can take hours or days to appear [3].

Keep her close and comfort her, and check on her regularly for changes in how she acts or feels [3]. Watch for a headache that gets worse or does not go away, repeated vomiting or nausea, unusual sleepiness or trouble waking, confusion or restlessness, slurred speech, weakness or numbness in the arms or legs, loss of coordination, or a pupil larger than the other [2][4]. In an infant or toddler, also watch for crying that will not stop and cannot be consoled, or refusing to nurse or eat [4].

If any of these appear, seek emergency care right away [4]. If her symptoms get worse, share this with your doctor [3].

q: is the MMR vaccine safe for my baby I read online it causes autism
text:
No, the MMR vaccine does not cause autism. Studies have found no evidence of a link between the MMR vaccine and autism, according to the NHS [1]. Many scientific studies have looked at this and found no link between vaccines and autism [5].

Vaccines are safe. They go through complete testing and safety checks before being approved in the United States [5]. The benefits of vaccines far outweigh their risks — the American Academy of Pediatrics, the National Academy of Medicine, and the CDC have all concluded this [3]. The MMR contains a live but weakened virus, so unless a child's immune system is weakened, it is unlikely to cause the illness it prevents [3].

If you are worried about your child having a vaccine, or are not sure whether they can have one, speak to your doctor or nurse [7].

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes

Hard, dry poop that hurts to pass is constipation, and in most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3]. The main sign is stool that is harder and less frequent than usual, sometimes with tummy pain, bloating, or a feeling of not having finished [2][4].

What helps most is more fluids, preferably water, and more fiber: cereals and wholemeal bread, fruit and vegetables [1]. Don't replace fruit with juice — juice has little fiber [1]. It's not essential that he poops every day; the rhythm and consistency of stools varies from person to person [1][3].

See your doctor if the constipation comes with bad tummy pain, blood in the stool, or repeated vomiting with refusal of food and fluids [1].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Most insect bites are harmless and usually just itch, and mosquito bites are no exception [5]. The bite should get better in a few days [1].

To ease the itching and swelling: put an ice pack wrapped in a cloth, or a clean cloth soaked in cold water, on the bites for at least 20 minutes, and keep the area raised if it's swollen [1]. You can use antihistamines to relieve the itching, and a hydrocortisone cream to reduce itching and swelling [1]. Do not let her scratch the bites, as they could get infected, and do not use home remedies like bicarbonate of soda [7].

See a pharmacist if the skin around a bite feels hot, looks red, is painful, looks swollen, or has pus or fluid coming out — they can recommend treatments such as antihistamines and steroid creams [7].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in several childhood illnesses, and the cause decides whether a nebulizer helps. Asthma symptoms — wheezing, coughing, shortness of breath, chest tightness — often come and go and are usually worse at night and early in the morning, according to the NHS [4]. Croup also causes a barking, seal-like cough that is often worse at night [5]. Whooping cough brings fits of rapid coughing, often worse at night, sometimes with a whoop or vomiting after the fits [1].

A nebulizer is not something these pages tell you to use at home. If your child has asthma symptoms, or has asthma and is waking at night or needing their inhaler more often, see your doctor [4]. If you think your child may have croup, ask for an urgent appointment — the doctor may give medicine to shorten the illness [5].

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
Your son needs fluids in small, frequent amounts, because the main risk of vomiting is dehydration [6]. Offer oral rehydration solution in small sips every few minutes rather than a whole glass at once, and keep breastfeeding or formula feeds going more often than usual if he takes them [7]. Do not give fruit juice, fizzy drinks or sports drinks — they have too much sugar and the wrong electrolytes [5][7]. There is no need to fast him: small, frequent amounts of his usual food are fine, avoiding fatty foods and sweets [5].

Get him seen today: vomiting a lot and not keeping down solids or liquids, or vomiting even when he takes nothing, are signs the SEUP says need urgent care [4]. Vomiting that is green, contains blood or looks like coffee grounds also needs urgent care [4].

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
text:
दस्त का इलाज ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) से किया जाता है — यह साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का घोल है, जो शरीर में खोए पानी और नमक की भरपाई करता है [1]। साथ ही ज़िंक की खुराक दस्त की अवधि को 25% तक कम करती है और मल की मात्रा में 30% तक कमी लाती है [1]। विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन के अनुसार, दस्त के दौरान बच्चे को पौष्टिक भोजन — जिसमें माँ का दूध भी शामिल है — देना जारी रखें, क्योंकि इससे कुपोषण और दस्त का दुष्चक्र टूटता है [1]। बच्चा खाना नहीं खा रहा है तो भी तरल और पौष्टिक आहार देते रहें [1]।

स्वास्थ्य विभाग, झारखंड सरकार के अनुसार, बच्चे को साफ कटोरी और चम्मच से दूध पिलाएँ, बोतल से नहीं, और खाना देने से पहले अपने और बच्चे के हाथ साबुन से अच्छी तरह धो लें [2]।

अगर दस्त लंबे समय तक बने रहें, मल में खून आए या निर्जलीकरण के लक्षण दिखें, तो स्वास्थ्य कर्मी से सलाह लें [1]।

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। खसरा आमतौर पर ज़ुकाम जैसे लक्षणों से शुरू होता है और कुछ दिन बाद दाने निकलते हैं; दाने आमतौर पर चेहरे के बालों की लाइन से शुरू होकर गर्दन, धड़, बाज़ुओं, टांगों और पैरों तक फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है [4]। चेचक में मुख्य लक्षण खुजली वाले दाने होते हैं, जो शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और दाने से पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार, दर्द और भूख न लगना भी हो सकता है [5]। हाथ-पैर-मुँह रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने निकलते हैं [3]।

अगर आपको लगे कि बच्चे को खसरा या स्कारलेट फीवर है, तो डॉक्टर से बात करें [1]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में मुँह और जीभ का सूखापन, बिना आँसू रोना, 3 घंटे या ज़्यादा तक पेशाब न आना, तेज़ बुखार, असामान्य नींद या चिड़चिड़ापन और धँसी हुई आँखें निर्जलीकरण के संकेत हैं, और यह जानलेवा भी हो सकता है [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत डॉक्टर की मदद लें [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को स्तनपान कराते रहें — दूध पीने की माँग हो तो सामान्य से भी ज़्यादा बार [1]। WHO के अनुसार दस्त का इलाज ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) से किया जाता है, जो साफ़ पानी, चीनी और नमक का घोल है [3]।

text: बच्चे के सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिसके लिए तुरंत आपातकालीन विभाग जाना चाहिए, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [1]। अगर गिरना एक मीटर से अधिक ऊँचाई से हुआ है, या बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा है, तो भी तुरंत अस्पताल जाना चाहिए [1]। रास्ते में बच्चे को आराम से लिटाए रखें और होश बनाए रखने के लिए उन्हें हिलाते-डुलाते रहें। अस्पताल में डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और तय करेंगे कि आगे कोई परीक्षण चाहिए या नहीं [1]।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
बच्चे का बहुत रोना कब्ज के कारण भी हो सकता है — कब्ज उन कारणों में से एक है जिनसे बच्चा रोता है [2]।

कब्ज में मल त्याग कठिन और दर्दभरा हो सकता है, इसलिए बच्चा पॉटी के समय रोता है। इस उम्र के बच्चों में रोने के और भी आम कारण होते हैं — भूख, गीला या गंदा नैपी, थकान, गैस, गोद में आने की इच्छा, ज़्यादा गर्मी या ठंड, ऊब या ज़्यादा उत्तेजना [3]। अगर समझ न आए कि क्या परेशानी है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करें [2]।

अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे शांत या ध्यान भटकाकर चुप नहीं करा पा रहे हैं, या रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है — ऐसे में डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें [4]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे का ठंड लगना, कंपकंपी आना और खासकर हाथ-पैरों की त्वचा का जालीदार दिखना सामान्य है — यह शरीर के तापमान बढ़ने की प्रक्रिया का हिस्सा है, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [2]। बुखार खुद कोई बीमारी नहीं, बल्कि शरीर के संक्रमण से लड़ने का संकेत है [1][4]।

बुखार उतरते समय बच्चा पसीना-पसीना होकर लाल और गर्म हो जाता है [2]। बच्चे को पर्याप्त तरल पदार्थ देना ज़रूरी है ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [1]। अगर बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो, तो डॉक्टर पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी बिना पर्ची की दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं; बच्चों को बुखार में एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए [1]। खुराक बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है — पैरासिटामोल और आइबुप्रोफेन के लिए PediBot का खुराक कैलकुलेटर इस्तेमाल कर सकते हैं।

banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन

जब तक मदद पहुँचे, बच्चे को खाना-पीना चालू रखने की कोशिश करें और बुखार हो तो गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]। बच्चे को माँ की गोद में या खटिया पर लिटाकर आराम से रखें [3]।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बहुत कम पेशाब आना पानी की कमी का संकेत हो सकता है, और अगर पेशाब गाढ़ा या बदबूदार है तो यह इसलिए भी हो सकता है कि बच्चा पर्याप्त पानी नहीं पी रहा [3]।

अब जो करें: बच्चे को बार-बार तरल दें, खासकर पानी, ताकि वह दिन में नियमित रूप से पेशाब करे और प्यासा न लगे [4]। अगर दस्त या उल्टी भी है, तो SEUP के अनुसार मुँह का रीहाइड्रेशन घोल (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दें, और खाना बंद न करें — सामान्य आहार छोटी और अधिक बार वाली मात्रा में दें; तैलीय चीज़ें, मिठाई और जूस से बचें, दूध और स्तनपान जारी रखें, और स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी कर रहा है, ठोस या तरल कुछ भी नहीं रख पा रहा, या उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफी जैसी भूरी हो, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन सेवा में ले जाएँ [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं

बड़े बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार के साथ बैंगनी दाग होना गंभीर संकेत है। त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लेने का संकेत हैं, और बुखार के साथ दाने निकलना भी चिंता की बात है [2]। ऐसे में बच्चे को बहुत ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े उतारें या स्पंज न करें — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है [2]।

दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए खुद कोई डोज़ न दें; डॉक्टर जो बताएँ वही दें [2]। 16 साल से छोटे बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें, और डॉक्टर के कहे बिना पैरासिटामोल और आइबुप्रोफेन बारी-बारी न दें [2]।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du

Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar hai — paracetamol bukhar aur bechaini mein madad karta hai, aur ise har 4 se 6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, NHS ke mutabiq [1][4]. AEPap bhi kehti hai ki paracetamol har 4-6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3].

Dose bacche ke wazan ke hisaab se tay hoti hai, umar se nahi — isliye apne doctor ya dawa ke leaflet se sahi matra lein [3]. PediBot ka dose calculator paracetamol ke liye maujood hai, wahan se wazan daal kar hisaab kar sakte hain.

Dawa dene se pehle bacche ko aaram dehne ke liye kapde kam karein, taral (liquid) dein aur activity kam karein [6]. Agar bacche ko 3-4 ghante baad bhi bukhar aur bechaini mein sudhar nahi hota, to agla antitérmico badalna uchit ho sakta hai — lekin apne paediatrician ki salah ke mutabiq [5].

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi bachchon mein asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabik khansi khaas taur par raat mein ya subah jaldi hoti hai [1]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki bachchon mein raat ki khansi ho sakti hai [3].

Ghar par: kamre ki hawa nam rakhein — saaf humidifier ya thande bhaap wala vaporizer istemal karein, aur bachche ko kaafi taral (paani, doodh) pilate rahein [5]. Sardi ki dawa ya khansi ki dawa apne aap na dein — kai cough-cold dawaon mein aise ingredients hote hain jo bachchon ke liye nahin hain, isliye koi bhi dawa dene se pehle doctor ya pharmacist se poochhein [5]. Aspirin bachchon aur kishoron ko bilkul na dein [5].

Turant madad lein agar saans lene mein dikkat ya tez saans ho, ya chehra, hont aur naakhun pale ya neele dikhein — yeh severe attack ke warning signs hain [1].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ho sakti hai — yeh uncomfortable hoti hai par aam taur par harmless hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jaati hai [6]. Iske symptoms hain chhote, ubhre hue dane, khujli ya chubhan wali feeling, aur halki sujan [6].

Ab kya karein: sabse zaroori hai skin ko thanda rakhna taaki pasina na aaye aur rash aur na bhide [6]. Dheele cotton kapde pehnaayein, halki bedding use karein, thande paani se nahayaayein, aur dehydration se bachne ke liye khoob paani pilayein [6]. Khujli ke liye thandi cheez — geela kapda ya ice pack (towel mein lipta hua) — 20 minute tak lagayein, aur khujaane ke bajaye rash ko thap-thap karein [6]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Agar aap sure nahi hain ki yeh heat rash hai, to doctor se poochein [6].

Agar bachcha sust ya adormilad lage, bahut pyaasa lage, aankhein dhansi lagein, bina aansu roye, ya peshab kam kare, to yeh SEUP ke mutabik urgent warning signs hain [3].

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text: Bacche ka kabz aam baat hai, lekin ise door karne ke liye aap kuch cheezein kar sakte hain. NHS ke mutabik, agar bacche ka pet saaf na ho raha ho to uske pet par halke haath se massage karein aur uski taangein cycle chalane ki tarah hilayein [3]. Agar aap breastfeeding kara rahi hain, to apne bacche ki positioning aur attachment sudharne se use aaram mil sakta hai [5]. Agar bacche ko dudh peene mein dikkat ho rahi ho ya wo bahut zyada ro raha ho, to apne doctor ya health visitor se baat karein [7]. Agar bacche ko bukhar ho, wo doodh peena band kar de, ya uski skin neeli, grey ya pale ho jaye, to turant emergency department se sampark karein [7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)
text:
Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai, aur ise halka nahi samajhna chahiye. Bronchiolitis mein shuruaat zukaam jaisi hoti hai — chheenkna, naak band ya behna, halka bukhaar — aur phir khansi, tez saans, doodh peene mein dikkat aur gharr-gharr ki awaaz aa sakti hai; yeh aam taur par din 3 se 5 ke beech sabse zyada hota hai [5]. RSV bhi pehle halka lag sakta hai aur kuch dinon mein badh sakta hai, jisme naak behna, kam khana-peena, khansi aur saans lene mein dikkat shamil hai [2].

Jab tak madad aa rahi hai, bachche ko seedha rakhein aur shaant rakhein, aur thoda-thoda kar ke tarral dena jaari rakhein agar woh le raha hai [5]. Agar bachcha doodh ya khana kaafi kam kar raha hai, ya 12 ghante se zyada peshaab nahi hua, to turant doctor se milna zaroori hai [5].

q: meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
Aapki beti ki susti aur jag na paana gambhir lakshan ho sakte hain. WHO ke mutabik sepsis ek medical emergency hai, aur bachchon mein iske lakshan hain tez saans, jhatke, phiki twacha, susti aur jag nahi paana [5]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki atyadhik neend ya bachche ko jagane mein kathinai ho to turant urgent dekbhal leni chahiye [4].

Jab tak madad aa rahi hai, bachche ko karwat par litaa kar rakhein aur uske saans lene par nazar rakhein [7]. Uske munh mein kuch na daalein [7]. Agar woh behosh hai lekin saans le rahi hai to recovery position mein rakhein [7].

Agar saans ruk jaaye ya woh behosh ho aur saans na le, to CPR shuru karein [7].

q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
तेज़ साँस लेना शिशुओं और छोटे बच्चों में ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या RSV का लक्षण हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस में बच्चा तेज़ी से साँस लेता है, साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ होती है और दूध या खाना छोड़ देता है [3]। CDC के अनुसार RSV शुरू में हल्का लग सकता है, पर कुछ दिनों में गंभीर हो सकता है; शुरुआती लक्षणों में नाक बहना, कम खाना-पीना और खाँसी हैं, जो आगे चलकर घरघराहट या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ बन सकती है [2]।

अभी बच्चे को सीधा और आराम से रखें, नाक साफ़ रखें, और थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दूध या तरल दें ताकि वह पानी की कमी से न रहे [3]। WHO के अनुसार पाँच साल से छोटे बच्चे में खाँसी या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ के साथ तेज़ साँस चलना (टैकीप्निया) या पसलियों के नीचे धँसाव निमोनिया का संकेत हो सकता है [6]।

रास्ते में बच्चे को गोद में सीधा रखें और शांत रखें [3]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common with whooping cough, an infection of the lungs and breathing tubes that spreads easily and can be serious [3]. The coughing bouts can last for a few minutes and are worse at night, and may make a "whoop" sound — a gasp for breath between coughs [3]. The cough may last for several weeks or months [3].

Keep the room cool and give small sips of fluid often. Ask a pharmacist about cough syrup or cough medicine, but some cough medicines should not be given to children under 12 years old [1].

Ask for an urgent appointment or get help from your local emergency number if your child has a very bad cough that is getting worse [5]. Get emergency help if your child's lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey, or if they are finding it hard to breathe properly [5].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text: A rash of red spots all over the body can have several causes in a 5-year-old, and the pattern matters. Measles rash usually begins as flat red spots on the face at the hairline, then spreads down to the neck, trunk, arms, legs and feet, sometimes with small raised bumps on top [4]. A spotty rash that starts on the head or neck and spreads to the rest of the body could be measles, and the NHS says to speak to a GP if you think your child has measles [5]. Measles usually starts with cold-like symptoms — a high temperature, runny or blocked nose, sneezing, a cough, and red, sore, watery eyes — followed by the rash a few days later [5]. If your child also has a rash that is swollen, raised or itchy, or swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, fast or struggling breathing, a tight throat, or becomes limp, floppy or not responding, these can be signs of a serious allergic reaction and may need immediate treatment in hospital [7].

q: should I give polio drops if my baby already had injection
text: No, the polio vaccine is not a repeat of the injection — the polio drops and the injected vaccine are different vaccines, and both are part of the schedule [2]. The six-in-one vaccine given at eight, twelve and sixteen weeks contains the injected polio vaccine, and the polio drops are given separately as part of the routine programme [2]. If your baby has missed any dose, contact your doctor to catch up; they will advise what your child should get and when [3]. It is important that vaccines are given on time for the best protection [3].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
It is natural to worry when a child refuses to eat, and it is common for children to refuse food or new foods sometimes [6]. What matters more is what they eat over a week rather than in a single day [6]. If your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they are likely getting enough to eat [6]. As long as they eat some food from the four main food groups — fruit and vegetables; potatoes, bread, rice, pasta and other starchy carbohydrates; dairy or dairy alternatives; and beans, pulses, fish, eggs, meat and other proteins — you do not need to worry [6].

Keep offering a variety of foods, as it may take many attempts before a child accepts some foods, and children's tastes change over time [6]. Give small portions and praise your child for eating, even if they only eat a little, and do not force them to eat [3]. Try to eat with them as often as you can, since children learn to eat and enjoy new foods by copying you [3].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A congested chest with a whistling sound in a 6-month-old can be bronchiolitis, which often starts like a cold and then brings a cough, faster breathing, trouble feeding and noisy breathing or wheezing, according to the NHS [2]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better in 3 weeks [2].

Keep feeding them little and often, and watch their nappies: fewer wet nappies or a dry nappy for 12 hours or more are signs they need help [2]. If they are struggling to feed or eat much less than normal, that also needs medical attention [2].

Wheezing is more common in viral infections, and a child with cough or difficult breathing is checked for fast breathing or the lower chest pulling in when they breathe in, according to the WHO [7].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में बुखार होने पर आमतौर पर घर पर ही देखभाल की जा सकती है, और तापमान 1 से 4 दिन में सामान्य हो जाता है [1][4]। बच्चे को भरपूर तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें — निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें, और रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखती रहें [4]। अगर बच्चा परेशान या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है, लेकिन पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा उसकी उम्र के लिए ठीक है [4]। 3 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें, और 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को भी न दें [2]। बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। अगर बुखार 39°C या उससे ज़्यादा हो, बच्चा खाना न चाहे या अपनी सामान्य स्थिति में न लगे, दाने दिखें, या बुखार 5 दिन या उससे ज़्यादा रहे, तो डॉक्टर से सलाह लें [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार में बच्चे को नहलाना या उसके शरीर को स्पंज से पोंछना नहीं चाहिए — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में भी न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ लें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखें, ऐसा विकासपीडिया कहता है [3]।

पैरासिटामोल बुखार के लिए दी जा सकती है, पर उसकी मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न के हिसाब से तय होती है [3]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को 5 किलो वज़न पर आइबुप्रोफेन न दें — NHS के मुताबिक 3 महीने से छोटे या 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन नहीं देनी चाहिए [7]।

अगर बुखार के साथ दौरे पड़ें, बच्चा खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से मना करे, सुस्त हो जाए, साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचें, सीने से कराहट या सीटी जैसी आवाज़ आए, या त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून या चेहरे पर नीली झलक दिखे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [3]।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ होना सांस की नली में रुकावट के कारण होता है, जिसे घरघराहट कहते हैं [2]। इस उम्र के बच्चों में इसका सबसे आम कारण सांस की वायरल बीमारी है [2]।

ऐसे में बच्चे को आराम दें और सांस लेने में तकलीफ बढ़ने पर तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [2]। अगर बच्चा ठीक न हो रहा हो या हालत बिगड़ रही हो, तो डॉक्टर से जल्दी मिलना ज़रूरी है [3]।

सांस लेने में गंभीर तकलीफ, तेज़ सांस चलना, पसली चलना, चेहरे-होंठों का पीला या नीला पड़ना गंभीर लक्षण हैं — ऐसे में तुरंत डॉक्टर की मदद लें [7]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
5 साल के बच्चे में बहुत खुजली वाले छोटे दाने स्केबीज़ (खुजली रोग) के कारण हो सकते हैं — यह छोटे कीड़े होते हैं जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं, जिससे तेज़ खुजली और दाने होते हैं [2]। अक्सर उंगलियों के बीच उभरी हुई लकीरें दिखती हैं जिनके एक सिरे पर बिंदु होता है, और स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही हो सकता है [4]।

इलाज क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवा से होता है [2]। इलाज शुरू करने के बाद बच्चा स्कूल जा सकता है, लेकिन पहले 24 घंटे दूसरों से नज़दीकी संपर्क से बचें [1]। इलाज कीड़ों को जल्दी मार देता है, पर खुजली कुछ हफ़्ते तक बनी रह सकती है [1]। दवा की मात्रा और तरीका डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर फार्मेसी के इलाज के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे, त्वचा में संक्रमण लगे या कोई और त्वचा रोग जैसे एक्ज़िमा हो [1]। खुजाने से त्वचा में संक्रमण हो सकता है [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। वैक्सीन्स के मामूली दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, लेकिन ये सभी टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का इलाज आसानी से हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर कर रही है [6]। वैक्सीन्स सुरक्षित, प्रभावी हैं और जान बचा सकती हैं [4]।

भारत में एमएमआर सहित टीकों के समय और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होते हैं — अपने बच्चे के टीकाकरण की जानकारी अपने डॉक्टर या स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता से लें [4]। अगर बच्चे की कोई खुराक छूट गई हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलकर उसे पूरा करवाएँ [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi asthma ke lakshan mein shamil hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ki khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [5]. Isi tarah SEUP kehta hai ki asthma crisis mein bachchon ko khansi ho sakti hai, kabhi raat ko [1].

Ghar par: kamre ki hawa saaf rakhein aur clean humidifier ya cool-mist vaporizer istemal karein [4]. Agar bachche ko bukhar ya takleef ho to SEUP ke mutabik aam antitérmicos (bukhar ki dawa) di ja sakti hai [6]. Kisi bhi cough ya cold ki dawa dene se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochhein, kyunki kuch dawaiyan bachchon ke liye munasib nahi hoti [4].

Turant madad lein agar saans lene mein sakht dushwari ho, hont ya chehra neela ya safed ho jaye, ya bachcha bahut bechain ya sust ho jaye [5][7].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ka bed se girna head injury hai, aur SEUP ke mutabiq aise mamle mein zaroori hai ki pehle 24 ghante tak nazar rakhi jaye [3].

Ghar par: agar sir dard ho to doctor ki batayi hui dose mein ibuprofen ya paracetamol de sakte hain [6]. Khana peena normal rakhein, koi khaas diet ki zaroorat nahi [6]. Baby so sakta hai, lekin zyada bade chot mein use har 4 ghante jagana chahiye [6]. 24 se 48 ghante aaram karayein, koi physical activity ya screen nahi [2].

In mein se koi bhi ho to turant emergency le jayein: tez ya badhta sir dard jo dawa se theek na ho, baar baar ulti, confusion ya behoshi, behad chidchidapan ya jagane par na uthna, bolne ya chalne mein dikkat, naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani [2][5]. 3 mahine se chhote bachche ya 1 meter se zyada unchai se girne par bhi turant dikhayein [5].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur WHO ke mutabik sarna (scabies) mein bhi sharir par dane aur khaarish ho sakti hai [1]. Sarna mein tez khaarish hoti hai, khaas taur par raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lakeerein dikhti hain; chhote bachchon mein hatheli, talwe aur sar ki twacha par bhi zyada gambhir dane ho sakte hain [1]. Sarna chhune se phailti hai aur iska ilaaj cream ya dawa se hota hai [4].

Agar bachche ko bukhaar, khansi, naak behna aur aankhein laal hon aur uske baad chehre se shuru hokar neeche sharir tak phailne wale dane aayein, to ye khasra (measles) ho sakta hai [2]. Khasra bahut sankramak hai aur isse bachav ka sabse achha tareeka teekakaran hai [3].

Dane khaarish ke saath ya bina, kisi bhi naye dane ke maamle mein apne doctor se dikhaiye taaki sahi kaaran pata chale aur sahi ilaaj shuru ho.

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai: bachche ko polio (VPI) ki vaccine 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar par lagti hai, aur 6 saal par ek booster bhi [3]. Vaccination samay par karana zaroori hai, isliye ise der na karein [3].

Agar bachcha kisi wajah se vaccine chhoot gaya ho, to bhi uski polio ki dose poori karni chahiye — doctor se mil kar pending dose lagwa lein [3].

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text: Diarrhoea after travel is usually an infection of the gut, and the main risk to watch is dehydration [6]. Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3]. See a health professional if the diarrhoea is persistent, if there is blood in the stool, or if there are signs of dehydration [1]. Signs of dehydration include much thirst, crying without tears, passing little urine or sunken eyes, marked irritability or drowsiness, and refusing to eat or drink [3].

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बड़े बच्चों में टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का टीका लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये दुष्प्रभाव आम तौर पर 2-3 दिनों में अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]। खसरे के टीके के 6-7 दिनों बाद भी हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं, जिनके लिए इलाज की ज़रूरत नहीं होती — ये लक्षण अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. के बाद बच्चे को पेरासिटामॉल की गोली या शर्बत दी जा सकती है, आमतौर पर टीके के एक-दो घंटे बाद; खुराक के बारे में टीका लगाने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें [5]। खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है।

अगर लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हों, या इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए, तो शीघ्र ही किसी स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी से परामर्श करें [5]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Dizziness is one of the symptoms of heat exhaustion, according to the NHS [3]. Heat exhaustion usually does not need emergency medical help if you can cool down within 30 minutes [3].

Cool your child down now and give them fluids [3]. Move them out of the sun, into a cool place, and have them drink cold drinks [2]. Loosen or remove extra clothing and sponge them with cool water.

Get medical help right away if they have a very high temperature, hot skin without sweating, fast breathing and a fast heartbeat, confusion or restlessness, a seizure, or loss of consciousness — these are signs of heatstroke, which is a medical emergency [4].

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text:
Solid foods baby ko taqreeban 6 mahine ki umar se shuru karni chahiye [2]. Shuru mein yeh zyada zaroori nahi ke baby kitna khata hai — ahem yeh hai ke woh khane ki aadat ho jaye; zyada tar energy aur nutrients abhi bhi doodh ya first infant formula se milte rahenge [2].

6 mahine se doodh ke saath saath mukhtalif qism ke khane dene se bachay ki sehatmand khane ki aadat ban sakti hai [2]. Aahista aahista miqdar aur variety barhate jayen, yahan tak ke bacha ghar ke baqi logon ka khana chhote hisson mein kha sake [2].

Agar bacha waqt se pehle paida hua ho, to solids kab shuru karni hain is par apne doctor ya health visitor se mashwara karein [2].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text: Loose stools are usually a sign of an infection in the gut, and the main treatment is to replace the water and salts being lost, according to the WHO [1]. Give your child oral rehydration solution (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — in small sips, more often than usual [1][2]. Keep breastfeeding or giving formula, and give small sips of extra water if they are on formula or solid foods; if your baby is under 6 months, boil the water first and let it cool [4]. Do not make formula weaker, and do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks, as these can make diarrhoea worse [4]. Keep giving their usual diet, including breast milk, during the episode [2]. Ask your doctor about zinc supplements, which shorten how long diarrhoea lasts [2]. See a health professional if there is blood in the stool, signs of dehydration, or the diarrhoea lasts 14 days or longer [2].

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text:
Yes, the MMR vaccine is safe. The NHS says research has shown there is no link between the MMR vaccine and autism [4].

Common side effects are usually mild and last only 2 to 3 days. They can include a raised, blotchy rash, feeling unwell and a high temperature around 7 to 11 days after the vaccination, and swollen glands around the cheeks, neck and jaw with aching joints around 2 to 3 weeks after it [4]. More serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are rare, and the person who vaccinates your child is trained to treat them immediately [4].

Protection starts within 2 weeks of the vaccine. After 2 doses, around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella, and around 88% against mumps [1].

The ages at which the doses are given follow India's national immunisation schedule.

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text: Yes, you can give your baby banana now that they have started solids. Introducing solid foods should start when your baby is around 6 months old, and at the beginning how much they eat matters less than getting them used to eating [4]. Offer a variety of foods alongside breast milk or first infant formula, which still provides most of their energy and nutrients at this stage [4]. Banana can be mashed or given as a soft finger food, and you can gradually increase the amount and variety as they get used to it [4]. Continue breastfeeding or first infant formula until they are at least 1 year old [3]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your paediatrician for advice on when to start solid foods [4].

q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text:
Watery stools with weakness in a 3-year-old is usually diarrhoea, which is loose or liquid stools three or more times a day [3]. It is common and often goes away on its own within a day or two [4].

Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — to replace the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. Also give zinc supplements: they shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

Contact a health care provider right away if there is a change in the child's mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, frequent loose stools, or signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying, according to MedlinePlus [2].

q: how do I know if my child is dehydrated from diarrhoea
text:
Signs of dehydration include being very thirsty, crying without tears, passing little urine, or sunken eyes, according to the SEUP [2]. Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness are also warning signs [2]. Another sign is stools so watery, heavy and frequent that the child cannot drink fast enough to keep up with the losses [2]. Refusing to eat or drink, persistent or intense tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood also mean you should seek care [2].

To prevent dehydration, give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado); Dificultad para respirar: respira rápido, «pitido» al respirar, se marcan las costillas
text:
Que se le marquen las costillas al respirar es un signo de dificultad respiratoria, y la SEUP lo incluye entre los motivos para consultar en urgencias [4]. También aparece como señal de que el catarro va a peor, junto con respiraciones rápidas o hundirse el pecho [2], y puede verse en la bronquiolitis, donde además cuesta comer y hay irritabilidad [3].

Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño tranquilo y en una postura cómoda, y ofrécele líquidos a sorbos pequeños si los acepta. No le des jarabes ni medicamentos para la tos sin consultar con su pediatra [7].

Aunque luego se ponga a jugar, el tiraje sigue siendo un signo de dificultad respiratoria y la SEUP recomienda acudir a urgencias para descartar complicaciones [4].

q: no hay quien despierte a mi hijo y respira muy raro
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: No responde a estímulos; Dificultad para respirar: respira rápido, «pitido» al respirar, se marcan las costillas
text:
No hay que esperar a nada: si no responde y respira mal, hay que actuar ya. Mientras llega la ayuda, ponlo de lado y no le pongas nada en la boca, según la SEUP [3].

La dificultad para respirar y los problemas para despertar a un niño son signos de alarma que obligan a consultar en urgencias [3]. Si respira cada vez más deprisa, se le marcan las costillas o se le hunde el pecho, es también motivo de urgencia [2].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre y rigidez en el cuello
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Rigidez de nuca: hay que descartar una meningitis ahora mismo
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico hoy mismo.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre y la rigidez de cuello son dos de los signos por los que hay que buscar atención médica de inmediato, según MedlinePlus [7]. La meningitis puede agravarse muy rápido [7]. Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño tranquilo y bien hidratado, sin sobreabrigarlo, y no le des nada por la boca si está somnoliento o no responde bien [5].

Los antitérmicos (paracetamol o ibuprofeno) alivian el malestar, pero no curan la infección, y su dosis depende del peso y la edad del niño, así que la indica su pediatra [5]. No bañes al niño en agua fría ni le pongas paños húmedos: resulta desagradable y no baja la fiebre [5].

q: mi hija se ha caido de un segundo piso pero parece estar bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Caída por las escaleras o de más de un metro, o llanto que no se calma tras un golpe: que lo vea un médico hoy
text:
Un golpe en la cabeza es un traumatismo craneal, y los síntomas más habituales son dolor de cabeza, confusión, pérdida de memoria transitoria, mareo, náuseas, vómitos y somnolencia [1]. Aunque la exploración médica no muestre alteraciones, se recomienda reposo físico y mental entre 24 y 48 horas, sin deporte ni pantallas, y volver después poco a poco a sus actividades [6].

Mientras tanto, vigile estas señales: dolor de cabeza intenso, progresivo o que no mejora con paracetamol o ibuprofeno; vómitos repetidos; desorientación o confusión; en niños muy pequeños, irritabilidad o dificultad para despertarlos; cambios en el comportamiento, dificultad para hablar o caminar; y salida de sangre o líquido claro por la nariz o los oídos [6]. También debe consultarse en urgencias si tiene un comportamiento o actitud que le preocupe [3].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre despues de vacunarse ayer
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre después de vacunarse es una reacción esperable y pasajera: la vacunación puede empeorar de forma transitoria el curso clínico, aunque estas situaciones son poco frecuentes [1]. El calendario de vacunación que se sigue en España es el calendario común del Ministerio de Sanidad [2].

No puedo darte una dosis: depende de la edad y el peso del niño. Para la fiebre, ofrécele líquidos con frecuencia y ropa ligera, y consulta a tu médico o al prospecto la dosis de antitérmico que le corresponde.

Si el niño está decaído, le cuesta respirar o la fiebre no cede, acude a tu médico o al servicio de urgencias.

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

text:
Según los patrones de crecimiento de la OMS (niño, 5 años):

q: mi bebe tiene 9 meses y todavia no tiene dientes
text:
La erupción de los dientes temporales empieza alrededor de los 6 meses, con los incisivos centrales inferiores, y sigue la secuencia habitual, según el Manual de Pediatría de la PUC Chile [6]. Que a los 9 meses todavía no le haya salido ninguno puede entrar dentro de esa variación normal, así que no hay que forzar nada ni preocuparse de más [6].

Mientras tanto, puedes revisarle la boca con calma: mirar los labios, la mucosa de las mejillas, las encías y la lengua, y aprovechar para empezar con el cuidado de la salud oral [6]. En esa revisión conviene fijarse también en el frenillo lingual, por si fuera corto y limitara el movimiento de la lengua, y en si hay problemas de oclusión dentaria [6].

Si te preocupa que no le salga ningún diente, coméntalo con tu pediatra en la próxima revisión.
sources: [6] PUC Chile — "Manual de Pediatría", section "FIGURA 7. TEST DE HIRSCHBERG FIGURA 8. COV

q: mi hija ha dejado de decir palabras que antes decía
text: Perder palabras que antes decía es una señal para actuar pronto, según los CDC: si tu hija no cumple uno o más hitos o ha perdido habilidades que ya tenía, no esperes [3]. Los CDC recomiendan hablar con el médico de tu hija, contarle tu preocupación y pedir una evaluación del desarrollo [3]. La Academia Americana de Pediatría recomienda cribados del desarrollo general a los 9, 18 y 30 meses, y de autismo a los 18 y 24 meses, o siempre que el padre o el profesional tenga una preocupación [3]. Si tú o el médico siguen preocupados, pide una derivación a un especialista que valore a tu hija más a fondo y llama al programa de atención temprana de tu zona para saber si puede recibir servicios [3]. Cuanto antes se empiezan los servicios de desarrollo, mejor es el resultado [5].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text:
El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no se debe a un problema del corazón, según el NHS [2]. Un dolor que aparece después de hacer ejercicio o de un golpe en el pecho, que empeora al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo puede ser un esguince o una contractura muscular [2]. La ansiedad también puede dar presión o dolor en el pecho, junto con palpitaciones, respiración acelerada o sudoración, según la SEUP [3].

Lo que conviene hacer es que descanse de la actividad que le provocó el dolor y que lo valore su médico, sobre todo si el dolor sigue o va a más [2]. No intentes diagnosticarlo por tu cuenta: si te preocupa, consulta a tu médico [2].

Acude a urgencias si el dolor es repentino y agudo, empeora al respirar hondo o al tumbarse, o si hay antecedentes familiares de infarto o angina en menores de 60 años [4].

q: mi hija de 13 años tiene reglas muy abundantes
text:
Las reglas abundantes son frecuentes y pueden ser normales, pero tienen tratamiento si afectan a la vida diaria [1]. Se considera que una regla es abundante cuando hay que cambiar la compresa o el tampón cada 1 o 2 horas, cuando se necesitan dos productos a la vez, cuando dura más de 7 días, cuando se expulsan coágulos mayores de unos 2,5 cm, cuando se mancha la ropa o la cama, cuando se evitan actividades diarias o cuando se nota cansancio o falta de aire [1].

Puede ser normal tener reglas abundantes, y a veces lo son en momentos concretos, como al empezar con la regla [4]. En algunos casos las causan problemas del útero o los ovarios, enfermedades que hacen sangrar más fácilmente o algunos medicamentos [4].

No siempre necesitan tratamiento, pero existen opciones que ayudan si afectan al día a día, como ciertos anticonceptivos o medicamentos para reducir el sangrado [6].

Conviene consultar al médico si las reglas abundantes afectan a su vida, si lleva tiempo así, si hay dolor intenso, si sangra entre reglas o después de relaciones sexuales, o si hay otros síntomas como dolor al orinar o al defecar [4].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Desmayo haciendo ejercicio, o con palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho: que lo vean en urgencias hoy
text:
El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, y suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. Después de un rato de reposo, los niños y niñas suelen recuperarse rápido, en un par de minutos [5].

Ahora que ya está bien, que se incorpore despacio: primero sentada y, tras unos minutos, de pie [5]. Conviene que beba más líquidos, sobre todo cuando hace ejercicio [4]. Si vuelve a sentirse mal, que se siente o se tumbe de inmediato y respire lenta y profundamente; si pierde el conocimiento, túmbala con las piernas elevadas y la cabeza de lado [5].

Hay que consultar en urgencias cuando el desmayo ocurre haciendo ejercicio físico o al hacer un esfuerzo, cuando tarda más de 3-5 minutos en recuperar el conocimiento, o si se acompaña de palpitaciones, dolor en el pecho, sacudidas de brazos y piernas o pérdida de orina [3].

q: mi bebe esta vomitando y no consigue quedarse con ni siquiera pequeños sorbos
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Vomita TODO lo que toma y no retiene nada: es signo de peligro, hay que verlo hoy
text: Que un bebé vomite y no retenga ni siquiera sorbos pequeños es una señal de que puede estar deshidratándose, y los bebés tienen más probabilidades de deshidratarse con los vómitos [6]. Ofrécele líquidos en cantidades muy pequeñas y frecuentes: si le cuesta retenerlos, prueba con sorbos pequeños de agua o trozos de hielo para chupar [2]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación dando soluciones de rehidratación oral ya preparadas, no soluciones caseras ni refrescos [5]. No le des medicamentos para los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [5]. Mantén la lactancia materna normal, e incluso más a menudo si el bebé la pide [4]. Según la SEUP, hay que consultar de nuevo en urgencias si el niño vomita mucho y no tolera sólidos ni líquidos, o vomita aunque no tome nada [4].

q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text: La fruta y la verdura pueden empezar a ofrecerse en torno a los 6 meses, cuando la leche ya no cubre por sí sola las necesidades del bebé [2]. Según la AEP, se aconseja introducir progresivamente toda la variedad disponible, en cualquiera de las comidas diarias, variando también la forma de presentación: triturada, chafada o en trozos pequeños [1]. No hay unas frutas mejores que otras para comenzar; la elección depende de los gustos de la familia [1]. Conviene introducir los alimentos de uno en uno, con intervalos de unos días, y sin añadir sal, azúcar ni edulcorantes [4]. Durante el primer año, evita las verduras de hoja verde con muchos nitratos, como acelga, espinaca o borraja [1]. Mejor fruta entera que zumo: el zumo no aporta ventajas frente a la fruta y aumenta el riesgo de caries [1].

q: mi hija de 5 años tiene granitos rojos por la tripa que le pican mucho
text:
Los granitos rojos que pican mucho pueden deberse a varias cosas. Unas manchas elevadas que pican pueden ser urticaria, a menudo por una reacción alérgica, y suele poder tratarse en casa [6]. Unos granitos muy picantes y elevados también pueden ser sarna, que igualmente suele tratarse en casa [4]. La varicela da un sarpullido con picor y granitos que van cambiando a ampollas y costras [5].

Mientras tanto, mantén las uñas de tu hija cortas y limpias para que no se rasque, y lávale las manos con frecuencia. Si el picor le impide dormir o está muy incómoda, tu pediatra puede indicarte qué le puedes dar.

Busca atención urgente si tiene hinchazón alrededor de la boca o le cuesta respirar [6].

q: mi hijo es asmatico y se le hunden las costillas al respirar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text:
El hundimiento de las costillas al respirar (tiraje) es uno de los síntomas de la crisis asmática: se les marcan las costillas y las clavículas y respiran más rápido de lo normal [4]. En un niño asmático, la crisis se produce por obstrucción de los bronquios y mejora con broncodilatadores como el salbutamol [2].

Lo que hay que hacer ahora: administrar de 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol, aplicadas de una en una, con una cámara espaciadora (y mascarilla facial en los niños pequeños), y repetir esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [6]. Los inhaladores deben darse siempre con cámara, nunca directamente en la boca [3]. Mantenerlo en reposo y evitar ambientes con humo [6]. Si van a un centro médico, llevar la cámara espaciadora [3].

Según la SEUP, hay que consultar en urgencias si la dificultad respiratoria empeora, si respira cada vez más deprisa, se le marcan las costillas o se le hunde el pecho, o si está muy agitado o somnoliento [3].

q: cuantas pufs de ventolin le doy
text:
La dosis es de 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol (Ventolín), aplicadas de una en una con una cámara espaciadora, y se repite esa misma dosis a los 10-15 minutos, según la SEUP [5]. En los niños pequeños, la cámara se usa con mascarilla facial [5].

Los inhaladores deben administrarse siempre con cámara, nunca directamente en la boca, porque así hacen menos efecto [3]. Si la crisis no cede después de este tratamiento en casa, o si te queda alguna duda, hay que acudir lo antes posible a un centro sanitario, sin olvidar llevar la cámara espaciadora [5].

q: cuanto apiretal le toca a mi hijo de 12 kilos
text:
Paracetamol para 12 kg:
• Dosis: 180 mg cada 4–6 h (máx. 4 dosis/día).
  – Apiretal, gotas 100 mg/ml: 1.8 ml
  – jarabe 120 mg/5 ml: 7.5 ml
  – jarabe 125 mg/5 ml: 7.2 ml
  – jarabe 150 mg/5 ml (3 %): 6 ml
  – jarabe 160 mg/5 ml: 5.6 ml
  – jarabe 200 mg/5 ml (4 %): 4.5 ml
  – jarabe 250 mg/5 ml: 3.6 ml
  – gotas 100 mg/5 ml: 9 ml
  – gotas 200 mg/ml: 0.9 ml
La guía admite de 120 a 180 mg; esta es la dosis habitual para la fiebre.
Fuente: AEPap — Guía rápida de dosificación práctica en pediatría (3.ª ed.), tabla analgésicos/antitérmicos.
Comprueba siempre la concentración del envase. Si tiene menos de 3 meses, consulta antes de dar nada.

q: y si no le baja la fiebre le puedo dar dalsy
text:
Sí, se puede cambiar de antitérmico si el paracetamol no mejora el malestar: si a las 3-4 horas la temperatura sigue alta y el niño sigue incómodo, es razonable dar ibuprofeno en vez de paracetamol la próxima vez, según la AEPap [6]. El ibuprofeno se da a la dosis que indique su pediatra, cada 6-8 horas [1].

Conviene recordar que los antitérmicos bajan la temperatura pero no siempre la bajan del todo, sobre todo si partía de una temperatura muy alta; que la fiebre siga después de un antitérmico es frecuente y no significa que sea más grave [3]. Lo importante es el confort del niño: mantenerlo bien hidratado, en una habitación ventilada y sin sobreabrigarlo [1].

Consulta en urgencias si está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable, si le cuesta respirar, si no tolera líquidos ni sólidos, o si le aparecen manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas [7].

q: mi bebe lleva todo el dia sin hacer pis
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Signos de deshidratación: ojos hundidos, orina poco, boca seca, vómitos persistentes o diarrea abundante >24 h
text:
Que un bebé pase hasta 24 horas sin hacer pis después de la primera micción puede ser normal, según la Junta de Andalucía [6]. Pasado ese tiempo, el bebé debe mojar los pañales con frecuencia, con orina clara e inodora, sobre todo si toma solo pecho [6].

Si el bebé está con vómitos o diarrea, ofrécele líquidos en pequeñas cantidades y a menudo, y mantén la lactancia materna normal o incluso más frecuente si la pide, según la SEUP [1]. No hace falta ayunar: puede seguir comiendo, en cantidades más pequeñas y frecuentes, evitando alimentos grasos, dulces y zumos [1]. En los bebés se puede usar la leche que tomen habitualmente, y en los mayores reintroducir su comida normal poco a poco [2].

Consulta de nuevo en urgencias si vomita mucho y no tolera sólidos ni líquidos, o si los vómitos son verdosos, con sangre o con aspecto de posos de café, según la SEUP [1].

q: mi hijo de 2 años tiene 39.5 de fiebre y las manos muy frias
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Manos y pies fríos en un niño con fiebre: puede ser mala circulación, hay que verlo
text: La fiebre es la respuesta natural del cuerpo a una infección, según MedlinePlus [3]. Con 39,5 ºC, lo que ayuda ahora es tratar el malestar con antitérmicos, ofrecer líquidos a menudo para evitar la deshidratación, no sobreabrigar al niño y mantener la habitación ventilada y templada, según la SEUP [4]. La fiebre alta no empeora por sí sola ni se vuelve peligrosa por el número [4]. No le des aspirina a un niño con fiebre [3], y no le des ibuprofeno si tiene menos de 3 meses, pesa menos de 5 kg, tiene varicela o está deshidratado, según el NHS [2]. Las manos frías con fiebre pueden indicar mala circulación, y el NHS incluye las manos y los pies inusualmente fríos entre los signos que requieren atención inmediata [2].

q: mi hijo tiene diarrea pero quiere comer normal
text: La diarrea con gastroenteritis no suele ser grave y el niño puede seguir comiendo si tiene hambre, según MedlinePlus [1]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación: ofrécele solución de rehidratación oral ya preparada, en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, después de cada deposición líquida o vómito, según la SEUP [3]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos para reponer las pérdidas [2]. No le des medicamentos para la diarrea o los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [2]. Consulta pronto si la diarrea dura más de un día en un niño, si tiene fiebre alta, vómitos frecuentes, heces con sangre o pus, dolor abdominal intenso, o señales de deshidratación como boca seca, orinar poco o no mojar los pañales durante 3 horas o más [1].
